The decrease in cost of sales for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily driven by a $22.9 million decrease attributable to lower volumes, partially offset by a $3.4 million increase due to loss of leverage.

nonop.text: Other income: Other income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $1.5 million, an increase of $0.1 million, or 7.0%, as compared to $1.4 million for the corresponding period in 2025. Other income is primarily comprised of interest income on cash, cash equivalents, and investments in both periods. Other income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $4.2 million, a decrease of $2.9 million, or 41.1%, as compared to $7.2 million for the corresponding period in 2025. The decrease in other income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to a $3.2 million gain on our investment in LifeMD common stock that occurred during the corresponding period in 2025. The Company sold its investment in LifeMD during the second quarter of 2025.

tax.text: Provision (benefit) for income taxes: The Company’s income tax provision for the three months ending September 30, 2026, reflects discrete items, primarily a $0.4 million change in unrecognized tax benefits due to finalization of a state tax examination, partially offset by $0.1 million of state income taxes. Income tax benefit for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $0.3 million, an effective tax rate of 1.8%, as compared to $0.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an effective tax rate of 14.9%. The decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily driven by the increased loss incurred during the three months ended September 30, 2026 and the valuation allowance on the net deferred tax assets. Income tax benefit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was less than $0.1 million, an effective tax rate of 0.2%, as compared to income tax expense of $1.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an effective tax rate of 174.4%. The decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily driven by the increased loss incurred during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and the valuation allowance on the net deferred tax assets, as well as various items in 2025 that were magnified by the near break-even pre-tax position.

net.text: Net loss: Net loss was $17.5 million, or $1.57 loss per diluted share for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to net loss of $2.3 million, or $0.21 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net loss was $22.7 million, or $2.05 per diluted share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $0.6 million, or $0.05 per diluted share for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The period-over-period changes were driven by the factors described above.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities decreased by $6.9 million to $5.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $12.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 primarily driven by a $20.2 million decrease related to changes in inventory balances and a $22.2 million decrease in net income, partially offset by a $16.7 million increase attributable to accounts payable and accrued expenses, a $10.8 million increase for non-cash restructuring charges excluding share-based compensation, a $6.8 million increase from income taxes, and a $3.3 million increase related to realized gains on the sale of investment securities.

da.text: In an effort to provide investors with additional information regarding our results as determined by GAAP, we disclose various non-GAAP financial measures in this quarterly report, our quarterly earnings press release, and other public disclosures. The following GAAP financial measures have been presented on an as-adjusted basis: cost of sales, selling, general and administrative expenses, income (loss) from operations, net income (loss), and diluted earnings (loss) per share. As-adjusted cost of sales, selling general and administrative expenses, income (loss) from operations, net income (loss), and diluted earnings (loss) per share exclude the impact of certain amounts related to Catalyst Restructuring efforts and have not been calculated in accordance with GAAP. We disclose Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, as a performance measure which excludes recurring items that we do not believe are indicative of our core operating performance: interest income, income tax expense, depreciation and amortization, and stock-based compensation expense, as well as charges related to our Catalyst Restructuring in the current period.

sbc.text: Adjusted EBITDA: Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes stock-based compensation and Catalyst Restructuring, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $0.4 million, an increase of $0.1 million, or 29.7%, as compared to $0.3 million for the corresponding period in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $3.3 million, a decrease of $9.5 million, or 74.0%, as compared to $12.9 million for the corresponding period in 2025.

wc.text: The Company had stockholders’ equity of $180.3 million and working capital of $160.1 million at September 30, 2026 as compared with $198.9 million and $158.7 million at December 31, 2025, respectively. The $18.6 million net decrease in stockholders’ equity was primarily driven by a net loss of $22.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, partially offset by $5.6 million for share-based compensation. The Company’s cash, cash equivalents and investment securities increased to $172.5 million at September 30, 2026 from $167.3 million at December 31, 2025.

intro.text: Medifast, Inc. (“Medifast,” the “Company,” “we” or “us”) is the 40+ year old health and wellness company known for its science-backed, coach-guided lifestyle system. As we enter 2026, the Company is moving from transformation to execution, leveraging its extensive experience in structured weight loss coupled with recent scientific research and enhanced product offerings to address the needs of a broader metabolic health market. Medifast’s approach focuses on addressing the root cause of metabolic dysfunction. This strategic shift targets a larger and more sustainable market, focusing on a long-term growth strategy designed to guide the Company over the next decade by aligning science, products, and coaching with increasing demand for new solutions as awareness of metabolic dysfunction grows.

gp.text: Gross Profit: In 2024, gross profit decreased $331.2 million, or 42.7%, to $444.6 million from $775.9 million in 2023. The decrease in gross profit was primarily attributable to lower revenue. As a percentage of sales, gross profit increased 140 basis points to 73.8% for 2024 from 72.4% for 2023.

cor.text: Costs of Sales: Cost of sales decreased $138.4 million, or 46.7%, to $157.8 million in 2024 from $296.2 million in 2023. The decrease in cost of sales was primarily driven by an approximately $123.9 million decrease due to lower sales volumes, $5.3 million decrease in inventory donations, and $4.7 million of efficiencies in inventory management.

oi.text: Income from operations: Income from operations in 2024 decreased $123.5 million to $2.9 million from $126.4 million in 2023 primarily as a result of decreased gross profit, partially offset by decreased SG&A expenses. Income from operations as a percentage of sales decreased to 0.5% for 2024 as compared to 11.8% for 2023 due to the factors described above in the explanations for gross profit and SG&A expenses.

ga.text: Selling, General and Administrative: Selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses were $441.7 million in 2024, a decrease of $207.7 million, or 32.0%, as compared to $649.4 million in 2023, primarily due to a $188.7 million decrease in OPTA VIA coach compensation due to lower sales volumes, a $13.8 million decrease in employee compensation, a $9.7 million decrease in credit card fees, and a $7.1 million decrease in costs for coach-related events. These decreases are partially offset by $22.9 million of customer led acquisition costs and $12.5 million of supply chain optimization costs. As a percentage of sales, SG&A expenses were 73.3% for 2024 as compared to 60.6% for 2023, primarily due to a 330 basis point increase for our company led acquisition efforts, a 330 basis point increase for loss of leverage on employee compensation, a 160 basis point increase due to loss of leverage on fixed costs, and a 200 basis point increase due to supply chain optimization efforts. SG&A expenses included research and development costs of $4.6 million and $4.6 million for 2024 and 2023, respectively, in connection with the development of new products and programs and clinical research activities.

sga.text: Selling, General and Administrative: Selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses were $441.7 million in 2024, a decrease of $207.7 million, or 32.0%, as compared to $649.4 million in 2023, primarily due to a $188.7 million decrease in OPTA VIA coach compensation due to lower sales volumes, a $13.8 million decrease in employee compensation, a $9.7 million decrease in credit card fees, and a $7.1 million decrease in costs for coach-related events. These decreases are partially offset by $22.9 million of customer led acquisition costs and $12.5 million of supply chain optimization costs. As a percentage of sales, SG&A expenses were 73.3% for 2024 as compared to 60.6% for 2023, primarily due to a 330 basis point increase for our company led acquisition efforts, a 330 basis point increase for loss of leverage on employee compensation, a 160 basis point increase due to loss of leverage on fixed costs, and a 200 basis point increase due to supply chain optimization efforts. SG&A expenses included research and development costs of $4.6 million and $4.6 million for 2024 and 2023, respectively, in connection with the development of new products and programs and clinical research activities.

tax.text: Provision for income taxes: For 2024, the Company recorded $1.7 million in income tax expense, an effective tax rate of 44.8%, as compared to $29.4 million in income tax expense and an effective tax rate of 22.8%, for 2023. The increase in the effective tax rate for 2024 as compared to 2023 was primarily driven by the 18.3% impact of state taxes and the 23.3% impact of the tax shortfall for stock compensation, partially offset by the 17.9% reduction from the impact of research and development tax credits, all of which were magnified by the near break-even pre-tax income position in the current year.

net.text: Net income: Net income was $2.1 million, or $0.19 per diluted share, in 2024 as compared to $99.4 million, or $9.10 per diluted share, in 2023. The period-over-period changes were driven by the factors described above in the explanations from operations.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities decreased $123.2 million to $24.5 million for 2024 from $147.7 million for 2023 primarily as a result of a $97.3 million decrease in net income and adjustments to reconcile net income to cash provided by operating activities.

wc.text: The Company had stockholders’ equity of $210.1 million and working capital of $150.2 million at December 31, 2024 compared with $201.5 million and $131.7 million at December 31, 2023. The $8.6 million net increase in stockholders’ equity reflects $2.1 million in net income for 2024 and $7.4 million for shared-based compensation offset by other equity transactions described in the Consolidated Statements of Changes in Stockholders’ Equity included in our consolidated financial statements included in this report. The Company’s cash, cash equivalents and investment securities increased to $162.3 million at December 31, 2024 from $150.0 million at December 31, 2023. In December 2023, the Company’s board of directors determined to change the Company’s capital allocation priorities and discontinued the Company’s quarterly cash dividend to support investments in technology and future growth. The decision to declare and pay dividends in the future will depend on general business conditions, the effect of such payments on our financial condition and other factors the Company’s board of directors consider relevant.

lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: No single customer accounted for 10% or more of our consolidated revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.

Jason Pharmaceuticals, Inc., our wholly-owned subsidiary with a manufacturing facility in Owings Mills, Maryland, manufactures our products, and accounts for approximately 40% of our total unit sales.
We manufacture and produce a portion of our products, which account for approximately 40% of our total unit sales, at our manufacturing facility in Owings Mills, Maryland.
Our business model does not depend on recruiting thousands of distributors who take on inventory to sell to clients.
The products underlying the remaining 60% of our total unit sales are manufactured by co-manufacturers in accordance with Medifast proprietary formulas and manufacturing standards.
Products manufactured by and programs marketed by the Company are sold under their own trademarks and trade names.
Our future growth and revenue depend upon the effectiveness and successful implementation of our strategic transformation plan.
Our future financial performance and projections increasingly depend on the successful execution of our strategic transformation.

If we are unable to reverse the downtrend of the number of active earning coaches, which has been declining since the first quarter of 2023, our future revenue and operating results will continue to be adversely affected, as we believe that the success of the Company depends on the success of our coaches.

Additionally, coaches are subject to high turnover, and we depend on our network of coaches to continually grow their businesses by supporting clients and attracting, training and motivating new coaches.

Our future success depends on our ability to continue to develop and market new, innovative products and to enhance our existing products, each on a timely basis to respond to new and evolving consumer demands, achieve market acceptance and keep pace with new nutritional, weight management, technological and other developments.
Our business depends on the effectiveness of our advertising and marketing programs, including the strength of the Company's and our coaches’ social media presence, to attract and retain clients.
Our business success depends on our ability to attract and retain clients.
We rely on third parties to provide us with a majority of the products we sell and we manufacture the remaining portion.
We also rely on third parties to distribute and deliver our products.
We rely on third-party manufacturers to supply a majority of the food and other products we sell.
We depend on frequent deliveries of ingredients and other products from domestic and foreign suppliers, especially for our non-powder products.
Some of our suppliers may depend on a variety of other local, regional, national and international suppliers to fulfill the purchase orders we place with them.

The availability of such ingredients and other products at competitive prices depends on many factors beyond our control, including the number and size of the suppliers that provide the raw materials that meet our quality and production standards.
We rely on our suppliers, and their supply chains, to meet our quality and production standards and specifications and supply ingredients and other products in a timely and safe manner.

Failure to take adequate steps to mitigate the likelihood or potential effect of such events, or to effectively manage such events if they occur, may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results, particularly in circumstances where an ingredient or product is sourced from a single supplier or location.
We rely on software, hardware, network systems, including cloud-based technology, that is either developed by us or licensed from or maintained by third parties to operate our websites.

In addition, our operations depend on our ability to protect our information technology systems against damage from third-party cyber-attacks, fire, power loss, water, earthquakes, telecommunications failures, and similar unexpected adverse events.
We rely on third-party software products to secure our credit card transactions.
We currently rely on a combination of trademark and other intellectual property laws and confidentiality procedures to establish and protect our proprietary rights, including our brand.
We rely on software, hardware, and network systems, including cloud-based technology, that are either developed by us or licensed from or maintained by third parties to maintain operations.

We conduct cybersecurity assessments of our key vendors before engagement, maintain continued monitoring during the engagement, and maintain the ability to discontinue our engagement with a key vendor if their cybersecurity posture fails to meet pre-established standards.

The decision to declare and pay dividends in the future will depend on general business conditions, the effect of such payments on our financial condition and other factors the Company’s board of directors consider relevant.
